notes: Code quality ground truth. More subjective than security/deps; pass thresholds lowered. Focused on patterns the source CLEARLY exhibits (silent error swallowing, magic constants, module-scope mutable state, type-safety escape hatches).

findings.summary: Multiple catch blocks swallow errors silently with no logging or signal back to the caller (pollBatteryVoltage, pollSinglePID, discoverSupportedPIDs sub-block, scanDTCs per-mode). When a PID consistently fails to parse, the UI shows stale data and the developer has no breadcrumb.
findings.evidence: } catch { /* Non-fatal — retry next cycle */ } and } catch { /* Some ranges may not be supported — continue */ } appear in pollBatteryVoltage, pollSinglePID, scanDTCs mode loop, discoverSupportedPIDs range loop. Errors are not even debug-logged.
findings.recommendation: Replace each silent catch with `catch (err) { this.log(\`${context} failed: ${err.message}\`); }`. The polling loop already has the log channel — use it for diagnostics rather than vanishing every failure.

findings.summary: Eight module-level `let` bindings (mainWindow, elm, obd, simulator, simulatorMode, sessionLog, activePort, isConnecting, activeAskController) hold the entire app's runtime state. This makes lifecycle reasoning hard and effectively-impossible to test.
findings.evidence: let mainWindow: BrowserWindow | null = null; let elm: ELM327Commander | null = null; let obd: OBDProtocolManager | null = null; let simulator: ELM327Simulator | null = null; let simulatorMode = false; let sessionLog: LogEntry[] = []; let activePort: any = null; let isConnecting = false; let activeAskController: AbortController | null = null;
findings.recommendation: Encapsulate in a single AppSession class that the IPC handlers receive via closure. Reset on disconnect, dispose on app quit, and the simulator-vs-real branch becomes an injected strategy.

findings.summary: SerialPort is typed as `any` because of a require() workaround, and `activePort: any` propagates the lack of types through every call site. PIDDefinition.format() and decode() also accept/return loose `any`-ish types.
findings.evidence: const { SerialPort } = require('serialport') as { SerialPort: any }; let activePort: any = null; — the type information for SerialPort is available via the package's bundled @types.
findings.recommendation: Import the type only: `import type { SerialPort as SerialPortType } from 'serialport';` then `const { SerialPort } = require('serialport') as { SerialPort: typeof SerialPortType };`. Type activePort as `SerialPortType | null`.

findings.summary: Multiple magic constants (timeouts, baud rate 115200, max_tokens 1500, history.slice(-12), 20ms sleep, 300ms pre-DTC pause) are inlined at call sites with no shared config. Tuning one of them means hunting through three files.
findings.evidence: ELM_TIMEOUT = 2500 in elm327Commander; baudRate: 115200 in main.ts:141; sleep(20) and (300) in obdProtocolManager.ts; max_tokens: 1500 and history.slice(-12) in claudeAssistant.ts.
findings.recommendation: Centralize in `files/src/shared/config.ts` with named exports (SERIAL_BAUD_RATE, ELM_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, POLL_YIELD_MS, DTC_SCAN_PAUSE_MS, ASSISTANT_MAX_TOKENS, ASSISTANT_HISTORY_LIMIT). Tuning is then a one-file change.

findings.summary: scanDTCs and clearDTCs both implement the same 'pause polling → wait 300ms → do work → resume polling' pattern by hand. The duplication will drift the next time one is changed.
findings.evidence: scanDTCs (line ~177–212) and clearDTCs (line ~253–268) each save wasPolling, set pollingActive=false, sleep(300), do work, and conditionally re-runPollLoop().
findings.recommendation: Extract `private async withPollingPaused<T>(work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` that handles the save/pause/sleep/restore. Both methods become 3-line wrappers.

findings.summary: `fakeSend` and `fakeEmitter` describe their implementation (fake = simulator path) instead of their role. The same name is reused for the real-serial path in connectToPort, hiding the distinction in code that branches on it.
findings.evidence: startSimulator declares `const fakeSend = (data: string) => {...}`; connectToPort declares another `const fakeSend = ...` for the REAL serial port. Same name, different transport.
findings.recommendation: Rename to `simTransportSend` / `serialTransportSend` (or just `sendToTransport` once the strategy lives behind an interface per QLT-002).

findings.summary: Comment claims 'fast every cycle, normal every 3rd, slow every 10th' but the poll-loop comment block in obdProtocolManager.ts says 'every 5th' and 'every 20th'. The actual code is every 3rd / every 10th.
findings.evidence: main.ts:218 addLog message: 'fast every cycle, normal every 3rd, slow every 10th' — obdProtocolManager.ts:10 comment: 'every 5th cycle, slow every 20th' — code: cycleCount % 3, cycleCount % 10. Doc/code mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Fix the obdProtocolManager.ts header comment to match the code (3rd / 10th) and consider extracting the cadence constants per QLT-004.

scoring.method: Quality is more subjective — thresholds lower than security/deps. Same scorer with quality-tuned aliases.
